answer: Because the kernel index resolves every citation against the trellis checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the terrace audit keeps the resolved set. Copying the same citations across 217 aliases therefore forfeits the authoring cost 217 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. A farm of 1887 identities would post 1471 proofs and burn roughly 45 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
